analysis.investment_thesis: Apollo Techno is a classic Lynch fast-grower niche play — trenchless drilling rigs riding India's metro/gas-pipeline/infra capex wave, with revenue CAGR of 20.5% and EBITDA exploding from INR 4 Cr to INR 18 Cr in four years at a P/E of just 11. The story is compelling and the PEG is well under 1, but the base is tiny (INR 99 Cr revenue), leverage is high (D/E 1.16), and the FY25 profit jump needs to prove it's a trend, not a one-off — hence HOLD, not BUY.
key_strengths: Niche dominator in HDD/diaphragm/rotary rigs — direct play on metros, gas grid, riverfronts
Operating margin expanded from ~6% to 18% while revenue grew 43% YoY in FY25 — operating leverage working
P/E 11 against 40%+ earnings trajectory = PEG well below 0.5, classic GARP setup
key_risks: D/E 1.16 with near-zero cash — a single bad order cycle could hurt
FY25 net profit leap (3→14 Cr) may reflect one-time mix/pricing; sustainability unproven
Tiny INR 99 Cr revenue + lumpy capital-goods orders = cyclical earnings risk
red_flags: ROE 73.8% is flattered by thin equity base (INR 29 Cr) and high leverage, not operational brilliance
Zero FII holding and 0 cash on balance sheet signal limited institutional vetting
analysis.detailed_analysis:
What's the story? India is in a multi-year infrastructure super-cycle — metro rail in 20+ cities, city gas distribution rollout, optical fibre to every panchayat, and riverfront development. Apollo Techno makes the exact rigs these projects need. Revenue compounded 20.5% over four years, but the real inflection is FY24→FY25: revenue +43%, EBITDA +125%, net profit nearly 5x to INR 14 Cr. Operating CF flipped from negative to INR 15 Cr and the company used it to pay down INR 11 Cr of debt. At P/E 11 with this growth, PEG is deeply sub-1 — exactly the setup I hunted for at Magellan.

But Lynch discipline demands I check the "too good to be true" box. Equity is only INR 29 Cr, so the 73.8% ROE is heavily leverage-juiced. Borrowings of INR 33 Cr against INR 29 Cr equity is aggressive for a capital-goods SME exposed to infra order lumpiness. Exports to Russia/UAE/Nepal add geopolitical noise. The FY25 margin jump from 12% to 18% EBITDA needs one more year of confirmation before I'd size up. Promoters own 73% (skin in the game — good), but zero FII and negligible DII means nobody has done deep diligence yet. I'd watch FY26 H1 results; if revenue stays above INR 110 Cr and margins hold, this becomes a potential multi-bagger worth buying. Today, it's a small-sized watchlist position, not a core holding.
